episodes.title: How the Mongols Kicked-off Modern History
episodes.description: In this episode, we explain what empires are and how they’ve created big changes throughout modern world history.

episodes.title: How Trade Revolutionized the Mongol Empire
episodes.description: Explore Mongol trade routes, including the Silk Road, and how commerce changed connections between societies.

episodes.title: The Fall of the Mongols and the Global Bazaar
episodes.description: Even as the Mongols disappeared into history, the trade networks that they helped develop continued to grow and evolve.

episodes.title: How Gunpowder Changed the World
episodes.description: Explore the influence of military technology and money on the development of empires.

episodes.title: Why the World Learned to Read
episodes.description: Examine how the printing press and increasing literacy transformed societies across Afro-Eurasia.

episodes.title: The Real Empires of the Americas & Africa
episodes.description: Examine empires beyond the familiar European and Asian examples.

episodes.title: Chasing Money and Power in the 15th Century
episodes.description: Explore how resource pressures encouraged fifteenth-century empires to expand.

episodes.title: How the Silver Trade Started
episodes.description: Explore the silver trade’s role in creating global networks and its consequences for empires and enslaved people.

episodes.title: Little Ice Age, Big Historical Consequences
episodes.description: The Little Ice Age caused famine, floods, drought, and disease that destabilized major empires.

episodes.title: How potatoes took over the world: The Columbian Exchange
episodes.description: Explore how diseases, plants, and animals moved between continents during the Columbian Exchange and the consequences of those transfers.

episodes.title: Riding the Waves of Oceanic Trade
episodes.description: Trace the growth of oceanic trade and its connections to economic expansion and enslavement.

episodes.title: Bitter History: Sugar and Slavery
episodes.description: Explore how the history of global consumption became intertwined with slavery in the Americas.

episodes.title: The Expansion of Silver Trade
episodes.description: Examine the challenges of early global trading networks in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

episodes.title: Charter Companies: The Original Monopolies
episodes.description: In the 16th century, seafaring countries wanted to dominate trade–so they formed chartered companies that helped empires expand their wallets and their borders.

episodes.title: Creole: The Creation of Culture
episodes.description: Explore how American, European, and African influences combined to create Creole cultures in the Americas.

episodes.title: Sparking the Scientific Revolution
episodes.description: Examine the Scientific Revolution and the new approaches to understanding the universe associated with European scientific developments.

episodes.title: Don’t Enlighten Me Until I’ve Had My Coffee
episodes.description: Explore the spread of Enlightenment ideas following the Scientific Revolution.

episodes.title: Revolution is Trending: Atlantic Revolutions
episodes.description: In the 18th century, new ideas about human rights and what is government led to revolutions– both violent and liberating!

episodes.title: Did Sheep Start the Industrial Revolution?
episodes.description: Explore the growth of industrial power within the eighteenth-century global economy.

episodes.title: What Drove Abolition in Britain?
episodes.description: Explore how religious ideas and free-trade economics helped fuel Britain’s abolition movement.

episodes.title: Human Rights Post Industrial Revolution
episodes.description: Explore how industrialization and new technologies intensified the exploitation of colonized peoples.

episodes.title: Wars for Global Resources: Opium, Poop, and People
episodes.description: Examine how industrial demand for resources and markets drove trade, innovation, and war.

episodes.title: What Makes Us Immigrate?
episodes.description: Examine the different forces that lead people to migrate.

episodes.title: How Nationalism caused WW1
episodes.description: Examine how nineteenth-century nationalism intensified international conflicts and helped set the stage for World War I.

episodes.title: What Set the Stage for the two World Wars
episodes.description: Examine alliances, nationalism, and industrialized imperial power as contributors to the world wars.

episodes.title: Life during World War
episodes.description: Examine war’s human costs for soldiers and civilians.

episodes.title: How Japan remembers World War II
episodes.description: Explore how Japan remembers World War II.

episodes.title: Who really fought the Cold War?
episodes.description: Explore how the Cold War became open warfare in formerly colonized countries as newly independent states sought their place in the world.

episodes.title: Are Modern Superpowers just Empires in a Trench Coat?
episodes.description: Consider whether imperial power disappeared after World War II or continued under different labels.

episodes.title: Globalization: How we got here
episodes.description: Explore how twentieth-century technologies fostered globalization and its unequal consequences for people and the environment.
